newsitem.title: USA: US CORPORATE BONDS-Boeing debt up, market sideways.
newsitem.headline: US CORPORATE BONDS-Boeing debt up, market sideways.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service increased the debt ratings of The Boeing Company on Thursday, causing prices on the airline maker's outstanding debt to rise modestly, traders said.
Otherwise, prices of most investment-grade bonds remained grounded on the day, changing little amid modest trading activity, they said.

The junk bond market continued to be dominated by new issue activity. Prices of oustanding high-yield bonds were quoted unchanged to 1/4 of a point higher, as the recent strength in equities continued to cheer bond investors.
Boeing senior unsecured debt spreads tightened one to two basis points on the news that Moody's upgraded its ratings to AA3 from A1, traders said.
Moody's also hiked the rating of McDonnell Douglas Corp senior unsecured debt to A2 from Baa1, causing their spreads to tighten by several basis points, a trader said.
Moody's said the upgrades were due to the positive effects of the ongoing merger between the two companies.
In other news, Burlington Resources debt widened by several basis points on the news the oil and gas exploration company planned to buy Louisiana Land & Exploration.
Rogers Communications Inc, Canada's largest cable television services provider, increased the size of its U.S. dollar-denominated 10-year debt offering to $330 million senior notes from $250 million.
That part of the deal (B2/BB-) was priced by Merrill Lynch & Co to yield 8.90 percent.

The company also increased the size of a seperate tranche of Canadian dollar-denominated 10-year debt to C$165 million from C$150 million. That tranche, sold (B2/BB-) by Scotia Capital Markets, priced to yield 8.75 percent.
Burlington plans to buy the company in a stock transaction valued at $3 billion.
Standard & Poor's affirmed Burlington's A-minus senior debt rating and placed Louisiana's BBB senior debt on watch for a possible upgrade.
But traders said Burlington's bond spreads widened slightly due to concerns its balance sheet may be weakened by acquiring a lower-rated company.
In the junk bond market, issuers sold roughly $1.0 billion in new bonds in five seperate deals on Thursday.
Among investment-grade new issues, Hilton Hotels Corp priced $325 million in seven-year debt to yield 7.045 percent.
The bonds are structured so that their yields will rise in the event Hilton's ratings are downgraded due to an acquisition.
Analysts said Hilton needed to provide investors with this protection as the company is currently mounting a $6.5 billion hostile takeover bid for ITT Corp.
In other markets, the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 18 points to close at 8,021, the day after its breached the 8,000 level for the first time.
U.S. Treasuries ended flat to modestly lower as late session profit-taking erased gains made earlier in the day.
The 30-year bond closed down 4/32 at 101-25/32, while its yield rose to 6.49 percent from 6.48 percent.
-Douglas Brown, U.S. Corporate Bond Unit, 212-859-1662
